intervals.label: laboratory in use (GeMSE installed)
intervals.note: Earliest document read that shows the laboratory in use (GeMSE paper of May 2015); the laboratory is older: all three GeMSE papers cite Gonin, Busto and Vuilleumier, Rev. Sci. Instrum. 74 (2003) 4663, which was not read.
intervals.quote: The setup will be installed in the Vue-des-Alpes underground lab near Neuchâtel (Switzerland)

name: Vue-des-Alpes underground laboratory
notes: Created for DELight, which names this laboratory as its phase-I host (arXiv:2512.15278); no Atlas facility existed for it. The only Atlas experiment placed here.
No official laboratory website was found; operator not stated in the sources read (the DELight paper says GeMSE is 'operated by collaboration members').

summary.plain: A small shallow underground laboratory in the Vue-des-Alpes road tunnel in the Swiss Jura mountains near Neuchâtel, under about 235 metres of rock. It houses the GeMSE gamma-ray screening facility and is the planned first-phase home of the DELight dark matter experiment.
summary.technical: Small underground space in the Vue-des-Alpes tunnel (canton of Neuchâtel, Switzerland) with 235 m of rock overburden (620 m.w.e.), electricity and network access only; hosts the GeMSE low-background HPGe screening facility (described by Freiburg- and Bern-based authors; the DELight TAUP 2025 paper says it is operated by DELight collaboration members); named as the phase-I site of DELight (TAUP 2025).
